title: Dualizing module of a nodal subcurve as an annihilator
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed [def-weil-field]. Let $X$ be a nonempty connected projective reduced $k$-scheme of pure dimension one whose singular points have completed local ring $k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-pc-scheme] [def-kun-projective] [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Let $i:Y\hookrightarrow X$ be the reduced closed union of a nonempty selection of its irreducible components [def-weil-closed-immersion] [def-weil-irreducible-components], and let $I_Y$ be its ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Then $Y$ is projective, reduced, pure of dimension one and nodal in the same completed-local-ring sense (a component boundary point can become smooth). Let $\omega_X$ and $\omega_Y$ be the duality modules of [lem-sfb-nodal-line-serre-riemann-roch], using that module on each connected component when $Y$ is disconnected. There is a canonical isomorphism
$$i_*\omega_Y\simeq\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(i_*\mathcal O_Y,\omega_X).$$
Evaluation at $1$ identifies this sheaf with the subsheaf $\operatorname{Ann}_{\omega_X}(I_Y)\subseteq\omega_X$ of sections killed by $I_Y$. Consequently, for every invertible module $M$ on $X$ [def-sc-invertible-module], the induced injective map
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_Y}(i^*M,\omega_Y)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(M,\omega_X)$$
has image precisely the maps whose images are annihilated by $I_Y$. Here pullback is [def-pc-module-pullback], the Hom sheaf is [def-pur-sheaf-hom], and $i_*$ is ordinary direct image of module sheaves. At generic points of $Y$ this inclusion is the canonical identification of the one-dimensional dualizing fibres; at the other component generic points its image is zero. Reducedness, pure dimension and connectedness use [def-pc-reduced-scheme] [def-weil-pure-dimension] [def-weil-connected-scheme]; algebraic closedness is [def-weil-algebraic-closure].

source.place: Tag 0E33 (lemma-closed-immersion-dim-1-CM), part (2); compare Tag 0E34 (lemma-closed-subscheme-reduced-gorenstein). Evaluation-at-one and the Hom image description unwind the displayed sheaf-Hom identification. Inheritance of nodality is the local branch calculation in Tag 0C4D (lemma-nodal).

proof.text: Choose a projective embedding $X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_k$. Composing it with $i$ is a closed immersion, so $Y$ is projective by the definition. Both $X$ and $Y$ are proper by projective-implies-proper, hence of finite type by the definition of properness. Reducedness of $Y$ is a hypothesis. Its irreducible components are exactly the selected components: each selected component is irreducible closed in $Y$, none contains another, and they cover $Y$. They all have dimension one, so $Y$ is pure of dimension one and is nonempty. The field $k$ is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0,k$); finite-type-over-Noetherian makes $X,Y$ Noetherian. They therefore have finitely many irreducible components. Connected components of $Y$ are the unions of irreducible components joined by chains of nonempty intersections; these form a finite partition into closed, hence also open, subsets. Denote their reduced open-and-closed subschemes by $Y_a$. Each is nonempty, connected, reduced and pure of dimension one, and its inclusion in $X$ is closed, so the same projective embedding applies to it.

source.place: Tag 0E38 (lemma-closed-subscheme-nodal-curve), opening reduction to component unions; projectivity and connected-component bookkeeping.

proof.text: Apply the nodal-subcurve boundary theorem with $N=X$ and the given reduced pure-dimensional-one closed subscheme $Y$. Its algebraically closed field, reduced finite-type source, pure dimension, and completed nodal local-ring hypotheses are exactly those verified above or assumed for $X$. It gives that $Y$ is nodal in the same completed-local-ring sense, and that a point on the boundary with the complementary subcurve is smooth on $Y$. Since $Y_a$ is open in $Y$, its local rings are unchanged, so every $Y_a$ is nodal as well.

For $X$ and each $Y_a$, the nodal Serre-duality theorem and the reduced-curve duality theorem give representing pairs for the identical functor $F\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_k(H^1(F),k)$. The uniqueness assertions identify these pairs canonically, preserving their duality isomorphisms. Apply closed-subcurve dualizing adjunction to $j_a:Y_a\hookrightarrow X$, using its nonempty proper reduced pure-dimensional-one hypotheses. It gives $j_{a*}\omega_{Y_a}\simeq\mathcal Hom_X(j_{a*}\mathcal O_{Y_a},\omega_X)$. Assemble over the finite disjoint clopen partition of $Y$: sections of $i_*\omega_Y$ and of $i_*\mathcal O_Y$ are finite products of the corresponding component sections. A homomorphism out of a finite product is uniquely the sum of its restrictions to the summands; finite products and sums of modules agree. The assembled isomorphism is therefore $i_*\omega_Y\simeq\mathcal Hom_X(i_*\mathcal O_Y,\omega_X)$. The component comparisons preserve the representing pairs, so the isomorphism is canonical for the specified duality data.

source.place: Tag 0E33 (lemma-closed-immersion-dim-1-CM), (2); Tags 0BS2 and 0BS3 for uniqueness of the representing pairs.

proof.text: Write $q:\mathcal O_X\twoheadrightarrow i_*\mathcal O_Y=\mathcal O_X/I_Y$. For every local module homomorphism $h:\mathcal O_X/I_Y\to\omega_X$, its value $w=h(\overline1)$ determines it, since $h(\overline a)=aw$. This value satisfies $I_Yw=0$. Conversely a section $w$ killed by $I_Y$ gives the well-defined local homomorphism $\overline a\mapsto aw$. These inverse constructions commute with restrictions, hence identify the sheaf Hom with $\operatorname{Ann}_{\omega_X}(I_Y)$. Evaluation at $1$ is thus an injective sheaf map $e:i_*\omega_Y\hookrightarrow\omega_X$ with exactly the asserted image.

source.place: Tag 0E33 (lemma-closed-immersion-dim-1-CM), (2); elementary evaluation-at-one description of sheaf Hom from a quotient.

proof.text: Pullback-pushforward adjunction identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_Y(i^*M,\omega_Y)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_X(M,i_*\omega_Y)$. Compose with $e$ to define the asserted map; its injectivity follows from injectivity of $e$. Every map in its image has values killed by $I_Y$. Conversely, if $f:M\to\omega_X$ has $I_Yf(M)=0$, its values lie in the subsheaf identified in the previous step, so $f$ factors uniquely through $e$. Explicitly on a trivialization $M|_U=\mathcal O_U m$, put $w=f(m)$. The map on $i^*M|_{Y\cap U}$ sends $\overline a\,i^*m$ to the unique section corresponding to $aw$ under $e$; it is well-defined because $I_Yw=0$. Uniqueness forces agreement on overlaps. This is the inverse on the claimed image.

source.place: Tag 0E33 (lemma-closed-immersion-dim-1-CM), (2); elementary factorization through the annihilator and module pullback adjunction.

proof.text: Let $\eta$ be a generic point of a selected component. Remove the finitely many other irreducible components of $X$ to get an open neighbourhood of $\eta$ contained in that selected component. On this open $Y$ and $X$ have the same reduced closed subscheme structure: the quotient ideal has zero radical in a reduced ring, hence is zero. Thus $(I_Y)_\eta=0$, and evaluation at $1$ identifies the included dualizing stalk with $(\omega_X)_\eta$ via $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O_{X,\eta},(\omega_X)_\eta)\to(\omega_X)_\eta$. The reduced-curve dualizing theorem says this is a one-dimensional vector space over $\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$. At the generic point of an unselected component, the complement of the selected union is an open neighbourhood disjoint from $Y$. There $i_*\omega_Y=0$, or equivalently $I_Y=\mathcal O_X$ and its annihilator is zero. This proves both generic-point clauses.
